name: Promising-ARM/RISC-V
description: A timestamp-based operational concurrency model for the ARMv8 and RISC-V instruction sets. It computes allowed behaviours incrementally from thread-local conditions, executing instructions in program order (bar early writes) without branch speculation, giving a substantially simpler operational presentation than prior ARM/RISC-V operational models. It reworks the timestamp/promise approach of the C/C++ Promising Semantics with a new uniform treatment of dependencies, but targets ISAs rather than C/C++, so it is a distinct model. Proven equivalent in Coq (for finite executions) to the axiomatic ARMv8 and RVWMO models.

catSupport.note: Despite its promise-based operational presentation, it is proved equivalent in Coq (for finite executions) to the axiomatic Armv8 and RVWMO models — that is, its behaviours are exactly those of herd7's aarch64.cat and riscv.cat. Unlike C/C++ Promising, its certification needs no value speculation.
